resources.string: Bixby button toggles the flashlight. While one of your chosen music apps plays, a quick press of volume up or down skips to the next or previous track; holding changes the volume. Only hardware key presses are seen; screen content is not accessible to this service. The Bixby button is detected from two system log tags.
Running in the background. Shortcuts work with the screen on or off.
Turn on SideKeys in Accessibility settings to use the shortcuts.
The flashlight shortcut reads the Bixby button from the system log. Grant access once from a computer, then turn the service off and on.
adb shell pm grant com.unl0cker.bixby android.permission.READ_LOGS

Track skip only works while one of your chosen apps is playing, and Android only tells apps with notification access which app that is. The same access lets SideKeys skip and seek in that app. SideKeys does not read your notifications.
Press the Bixby button to turn the flashlight on or off.
While one of your chosen apps plays, a quick press of volume up or down skips to the next or previous track. Hold to change the volume.

resources.string: Track skip works while a checked app is the one playing. Anything else, such as videos, voice notes or audiobooks, keeps normal volume keys.
How long to hold a volume key before it changes the volume instead of skipping.
Tap a volume key, then press and hold it: up seeks forward, down seeks back. A single tap then skips after a short pause.
How fast the track slides while you hold: at 8×, one second of holding moves eight seconds through the track.
The longer you hold, the faster it goes: the seek speed doubles every 2 seconds, up to 8 times.
